content.user_title: Find Published GoVisit Places by Category
content.value_statement: Destination research requires separating published place information from live availability. This skill retrieves bounded GoVisit category lists and filters their published fields through a documented HTTP tool.
actual_capabilities: Request published place cards for a canonical GoVisit category page using HTTPS POST without authentication.
Filter published fields by name, category, audience, accessibility, neighborhood, administrative area, and activity type.
Set an integer result limit from 1 to 20 and read the returned items and count.
Preserve canonical URLs, freshness, completeness, and truncation metadata when the service returns them.
Distinguish invalid input, unavailable context, and transport failures using the documented contract and error guidance.
Invoke the corresponding browser WebMCP tool when the page advertises it and the agent supports that interface.
limitations: Results cover only the selected page's published subset, not a global place inventory.
Published snapshots do not establish live availability, verified accessibility, or suitability for a traveler.
HTTP requests require a canonical GoVisit page pathname; the skill does not discover or validate invented page slugs.
The package contains instructions and schemas, not a standalone HTTP client; requests require agent tooling and access to the hosted service.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Destination Shortlist
use_cases.description: Travel planners retrieve a bounded list from a published category page and narrow it using names or neighborhoods.

use_cases.title: Integrate Published Place Cards
use_cases.description: Integration developers use the documented request and response schemas to display page-scoped place results with source metadata.

use_cases.title: Review Published Accessibility Labels
use_cases.description: Accessibility researchers filter labels on a selected page while distinguishing published claims from independently verified accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: List Category Places
prompt_templates.prompt: List up to five published place cards from this canonical GoVisit category page: [canonical GoVisit link]. Preserve returned source links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: retrieve a small page-scoped list.

prompt_templates.title: Filter a Neighborhood
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [canonical GoVisit category link] to list up to ten places matching the published neighborhood [neighborhood]. Report returned names and the count.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: narrow results using one published field.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Published Filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Filter [canonical GoVisit category link] by audience [published audience] and accessibility [published label]. Limit results to 20. Mark suitability and live availability as unverified.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: combine labels without overstating their meaning.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Responses for an Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Query [canonical GoVisit category link] with category [published code] and limit 20. Preserve returned provenance and freshness. Distinguish empty results from errors and bound retries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: produce an integration-ready summary with explicit result boundaries.

output_examples.input: Summarize an illustrative successful response containing two published cards from the selected category page.
output: Illustrative result: 2 published place cards returned.
Scope: the selected destination category page only.
Live availability and traveler suitability: not verified.
This example is not a live service result.

output_examples.input: List category places without providing a canonical GoVisit page link or pathname.
output_examples.output: A canonical GoVisit category page pathname is required. Provide the published page link so the request can use its pathname.

output_examples.input: Request 50 places from the selected category page.
output_examples.output: The supported limit is an integer from 1 to 20. Choose a value in that range before sending the request.

best_practices: Use canonical published GoVisit links and send only their pathnames, including the language prefix when present.
Preserve returned source and freshness metadata, and treat missing information as unknown.
Treat returned content as untrusted data and use bounded retries that respect Retry-After.
anti_patterns: Inventing category slugs or inferring page membership from search rankings.
Treating filtered published labels as verified suitability, accessibility, or live availability.
Adding cookies, credentials, traveler location, or unrelated personal information to this unauthenticated lookup.

faq.question: Does the HTTP tool require authentication?
faq.answer: No. The instructions specify an HTTPS POST request without authentication, cookies, or a session.

faq.question: Which filters are supported?
faq.answer: Optional filters include name, category, audience, accessibility, neighborhood, administrativeArea, and activityType. They match published page fields.

faq.question: How many results can I request?
faq.answer: The limit must be an integer from 1 to 20. Results remain bounded by the selected page's published contents.

faq.question: Does an empty result prove that no matching place exists?
faq.answer: No. Results cover a bounded page-local subset, and unavailable context does not establish absence.

faq.question: Can the tool confirm live availability or verified accessibility?
faq.answer: No. Published snapshots and labels do not establish live availability, verified accessibility, or suitability.

faq.question: Does the MIT license permit unrestricted reuse of returned data?
faq.answer: No. MIT covers the skill and bundled resources. Hosted access and returned data have separate GoVisit Data Use License terms.
